name: redis-operator-content-addressed-94ed
instr:
Make referenced Redis configuration content part of workload identity so Secret and ConfigMap changes reliably trigger rollouts without requiring custom resource edits. Standalone, cluster, replication, and Sentinel resources should expose both the revision they want and the revision their workloads have actually reached. Existing topology behavior, connection information, and workload parameters must remain compatible.

A configuration dependency has canonical kind, namespace, name, and selected-key identity, and each topology reports exactly the dependencies its workloads consume. `ConfigDependencyKind`, `ConfigDependency`, `ConfigRevision`, `ConfigRevisionStatus`, and `RevisionError` are provided by `github.com/OT-CONTAINER-KIT/redis-operator/api/common/v1beta2`; resolution returns the exact selected bytes together with Kubernetes resource identity, and failures identify their dependency and distinguish a missing selected key from an unavailable object. `ResolveConfigRevision` from `github.com/OT-CONTAINER-KIT/redis-operator/internal/configrevision` hashes only selected bytes and resource identity into a deterministic, order-independent revision, including a stable empty revision. Every affected pod template carries the operator-managed desired revision, which survives annotation filtering and StatefulSet patching while immutable or allocated fields remain intact.
